name: Imran Khan
role: Pakistani cricketer, founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) and Prime Minister of Pakistan (2018-2022); imprisoned since 2023
summary: Khan combines anti-corruption and anti-elite populism with an Islamic welfare-state vision modelled on Medina, expanded poverty programmes (Ehsaas, Sehat Sahulat) and a pro-private-sector growth agenda. He defends Pakistan's blasphemy laws, pursues an independent foreign policy tilted to China and refuses US bases, and has been critical of army interference in politics since his 2022 removal. His remarks on women's dress and the Taliban takeover drew heavy criticism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme says Pakistan needs an effective defence capacity and strengthened deterrent.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: The programme proposes raising the share of direct taxes.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The programme reforms the police into a service-oriented force rather than abolishing it.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The programme gives households land ownership.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He calls India's 2019 annexation of Kashmir illegal and likens it to Munich 1939, with a UN plebiscite required.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He calls resisting foreign occupation jihad, says Afghan mujahideen were freedom fighters, and that he'd pick up a gun in Kashmir.

central-bank-independence.rationale: His government's IMF programme committed to strengthen State Bank autonomy and end central bank deficit financing.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: His book says the Quran prohibits murder and condemns 9/11 as terrorism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: His book says imposing an alien culture on a people brought destruction and that colonialism rests on a claim of superiority.

clerical-rule.rationale: His book criticises reactionary mullahs and calls the Taliban's theocracy an unenlightened version of Islam.

close-ties-china.rationale: He praised China as a partner and model, while wanting a balanced relationship with the US.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His 2025 op-ed says Pakistan should be a democratic system chosen by the people.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: His book calls for an alternative to the Western materialism and consumerism the ruling classes imbibed.

death-penalty.rationale: He called for hanging rapists and child abusers in public and his book backs capital punishment for large-scale corruption.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He wants a welfare state on the Medina model taking responsibility for the weak.

decide-locally.rationale: He proposes citizen boards and directly funded local government, and in his book urges reviving panchayat and jirga councils.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: He says jihad means fighting foreign occupation and that fighters in Afghanistan and elsewhere act in the name of Islam against injustice.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The programme says Pakistan must not bend to alien interests, and he refused US bases.

democracy-best.rationale: He praised the Chinese one-party model as beating Western democracies, while also stating that democracy chosen by the people is the way forward.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He demands a UN plebiscite for Kashmir's people to decide.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: His book endorses the Prophet's last sermon: no people is superior to another except by piety.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He calls climate change an existential threat and listed a ten-billion-tree drive, renewables and ending coal in his UN speech.

dynastic-succession.rationale: His book says family dynasties in politics lead to incompetence and are worse than monarchy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The programme pledges to remove draconian laws and he calls military trials of civilians a rights violation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He says the law must be the same for everyone, that the Prophet declared every person equal before the law, and calls discrimination on race, religion or class un-Islamic.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme backs local coal and oil extraction, while his UN speech rules out power from coal.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The programme states that the nuclear power programme will be expanded.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: His book stresses fair trials and condemns extrajudicial killing and drone strikes.

farm-price-support.rationale: The programme links crop prices to input costs and sets up crop and livestock insurance.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The programme calls for laws setting guidelines and a limit on new debt.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: He told Modi to resolve differences through trade and trust.

future-generations.rationale: The programme and his book commit to sustainable use so future generations are not shortchanged.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: He called for a global dialogue and interfaith harmony efforts.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: He says rich countries mainly responsible for greenhouse-gas emissions must do more.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He says Pakistan cannot achieve self-esteem while dependent on international aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The programme pledges to strengthen the country's nuclear deterrent and missiles.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He wants Western democracy blended with panchayat-style local government and called the Chinese party model unique, rather than copying the West.

islam-incompatible.rationale: His book says a true Islamic society differs from European welfare states little beyond family provisions, but rejects Western moral values.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The programme pledges to strengthen the nuclear deterrent.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He holds that the Quran is the foundation of a just society and that sharia should be rebuilt through ijtihad.

limit-growth.rationale: His book says a humane Islamic society would sacrifice growth to protect the environment, while the programme targets at least 8 percent annual growth.

limit-population.rationale: The programme commits to cutting population growth from 2.2 to 1.6 percent through family planning campaigns.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He says the army must respect constitutional limits, yet that it is foolish to think the army will have no role in governance.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: His book says concentration of power at the centre negated federalism for Pashtuns, Baluchis and Sindhis.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The programme encourages public-private partnership in health, education and railways.

more-religion-public.rationale: His government added a Seerat course for grades 8-10 and religious teaching to the national curriculum.

nation-first.rationale: He insists on an independent foreign policy and refused US bases, but also says climate and illicit finance need a combined global effort.

national-rebirth.rationale: His book calls for a cultural, intellectual and moral renaissance and a soft revolution against the corrupt order.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He says the state must take responsibility for the weak, as in Medina, and promised policies for the poor.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The programme will eliminate tax exemptions that benefit special interests.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He says he would never have agreed to US bases and described refusing them.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: His government's national curriculum adds a Seerat course and religious teaching, including minority faiths, in state schools.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He praises the Medina state for taxing the rich to spend on the poor.

office-by-exam.rationale: The programme puts civil service recruitment through autonomous public service commissions with exam reform.

one-party-rule.rationale: He frames his cause as a fight for free elections and a democracy chosen by the people.

open-government-data.rationale: The programme promises transparency in government and wider public access to information.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme creates citizen and community boards, and his book urges reviving village councils to empower people.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: At the UN and in his book he describes ruling elites as plundering their own countries and looting the state.

population-transfer.rationale: He condemns the ethnic cleansing of Muslims in Myanmar and the RSS belief in it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The programme says the diversity of culture and traditions must flourish and promises a heritage-protection policy; he warned against adopting another culture.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He promised that policies would be for the poor and weaker classes, and made poverty the programme's highest priority.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He promises supremacy of law and equal law for all, and the programme seeks an independent judiciary.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The programme aims to reduce population growth through national campaigns.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The programme says to widen public access to information by revising confidentiality laws.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He said there would be no compromise on blasphemy laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: His book endorses the Prophet's last sermon rejecting superiority by race.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: His book states discrimination on race, religion or class is prohibited by the Quran.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: His government accepted the 2019 IMF programme with fiscal consolidation conditions.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The programme calls for provincial autonomy as the constitution intends.

rehabilitation.rationale: The programme says jails should function as correction centres and end police torture.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: His book backs Iqbal's call for ijtihad so each generation can reinterpret Islamic law for its time.

religion-illusion.rationale: His book describes faith as the thing that transformed his life and the basis of a just society.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: He rebuts the claim that Islam is against women, saying Medina cared for the weak.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: He condemns Western moves against the hijab as Islamophobia.

religious-nation.rationale: His book calls Islam and the Two-Nation Theory the bedrock of Pakistan's foundations.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: His book cites 'no compulsion in religion' and says religion is won by hearts, not force.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: He condemns ethnic cleansing as practised on Rohingya and Indian Muslims.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: The programme calls for working-class representation in assemblies.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: He says Pakistan would fight to the death for freedom and cites Iqbal on death before a servile life.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He urges legal safeguards protecting religious sensitivities and action against Islamophobia.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: His UN speech asks for debt restructuring, more aid, SDR reallocation and curbs on tax havens.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: His UN speech asks for expanded aid, while his book calls aid a crutch and says the West's best gift is returning looted money.

rich-first.rationale: The programme criticises a resource formula that condemns regions to poverty and calls for equitable sharing.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: His 2025 op-ed demands a judicial commission to investigate attacks by security services on his party's workers.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: His government took a US$6 billion IMF programme and Fund support.

separate-church-state.rationale: His book says an Islamic state cannot be secular because Islam has no church, and quotes Iqbal that the dualism does not exist in Islam.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme seeks an independent judiciary, parliamentary scrutiny of the defence budget and a civilian army under constitutional bounds.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: He says he never understood why tax havens exist and urges the UN to shut the flows.

simple-living.rationale: His book questions chasing nightclubs and designer clothes and the programme calls for simple living.

social-market-economy.rationale: He backs private-sector wealth creation with a welfare safety net, as stated in the programme and victory speech.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He says no one was above the law in Medina and promises equal law for all, starting with himself.

spiritual-nature.rationale: His book quotes Gandhi that religion belongs in politics and warns a Godless state breeds materialism.

state-harmful.rationale: He wants stronger state institutions and a welfare state on the Medina model, which excludes abolishing the state.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: His government issued an ordinance extending criminal defamation penalties online.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: His government expanded religious content in state curricula.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: His book says an Islamic state protects marriage and shields the young from public immorality.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He says Pakistan should be a friend to all and no one's proxy, and told the government to stay neutral after 9/11.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The programme wants more direct taxation of wealth and capital gains, yet also a flatter system at lower rates, so it points both ways.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme asks citizens to share part of their income as tax, and he links tax-paying to honest government.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: His book follows Iqbal in using Western science without subordinating to Western values.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: The programme says to eliminate police torture.

total-state.rationale: The programme limits the government's role in the economy to enabling wealth creation.

traditional-family.rationale: His book calls the family structure the net that keeps society intact and the programme says family values bind society.

unions-good.rationale: The programme promises all rights tied to trade union activity and repeal of repressive labour laws.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The programme he led sets the goal of adequate health services for all citizens, with low-cost insurance for the poor and elderly.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: His book says zealots enforcing Islam at gunpoint have done tremendous damage and that religion is a battle for hearts and minds.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme proposes land reform so most rural households own a minimum plot and ownership of assets for the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: His book follows Iqbal in saying that turning away from the real world is contrary to the spirit of Islam.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme gives women a level playing field for social, political and economic growth.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He argues billions leave poor countries every year to rich ones, deepening poverty and widening the gap.

notes: Second pass, brought up to rules 7. The first pass leaned on Wikipedia and news summaries; this pass answers from his own words (UN speeches 2019 and 2021, his 2011 book read in a third-party scanned copy, the 2018 victory speech, his 2025 TIME op-ed), a PTI programme (the SlideShare copy posted as the 2018 manifesto is an older text, written in the Musharraf era) and records (IMF programme, curriculum, 2022 PECA ordinance). Themes searched: economy, society, government, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology. Government and world are the best covered; means, technology and most economy-theory statements have no stated position and stay null. Records noted but not settling any statement: removal of the Ahmadi economist Atif Mian from the Economic Advisory Council (Sept 2018), Army chief tenure extension law (Jan 2020), and the April 2022 dissolution advice ruled unconstitutional by the Supreme Court. His relationship to the army changed after 2022. Views on the US before and after 2022 are not used for any answer. Wikipedia sources from the first pass remain listed only because earlier versions of changed answers cite them in reviewHistory.
